## Summary

Kuno von Liebenstein, komtur of Osterode and godfather of Danutė, is the Order's informant who warned [Kęstutis](kestutis.qmd) of the secret treaty of [Dovydiškės](../events/ev_dovydiskes.qmd) in August 1381. He is named in Book I ch. 1.

## Appearance & tells

Not described: the books give him one sentence and no face. Book I ch. 1 names him as the komtur of Osterode who warned Kęstutis "in whispers" of the Dovydiškės treaty, and the saga leaves him there, an Order officer with a conscience whose entire role is a whisper in August 1381. His only "tell" is that he acts as a friend across the lines: as godfather to Kęstutis's daughter Danutė (the record) he owes the family a loyalty that the Order's rule does not recognise.

## Want · Need · Lie · Truth

| | |
|---|---|
| **Want** (external) | (The books give no stated aims.) To protect his goddaughter's family from a treachery he knew of, and to keep Kęstutis alive as a counterweight to Jogaila. |
| **Need** (internal) | To act on the Order's word of honour or his godparent's obligation: to decide where his loyalty lies. |
| **Lie** they believe | The Order's secret deals are not his to reveal. |
| **Truth** they learn (or refuse) | He reveals one: Kęstutis learns the treaty of Dovydiškės and seizes Vilnius in autumn 1381. |

## Arc by book

- **Book I (Aug 1381, ch. 1).** Warns Kęstutis in a whisper of the secret treaty of Dovydiškės between Jogaila and the Order; on that warning Kęstutis takes Vilnius with three days' ride, reads the treaty, and releases Jogaila, the mercy that kills him in 1382.
- **Book VI.** Not on page: the afterword explains that the 1381 warning belongs to the historical Liebenstein, while the invented young brother Günther von Hohenstein, who admires Kęstutis in Book VI, is not the informant.

## Power & magic

**Tier 0**; no powers and no role in the magic. Only a name and a warning.

## Record vs saga

- **[Record]:** Ivinskis (1978), followed by the English Wikipedia (Civil War 1381-84; Treaty of Dovydiškės): Kuno von Liebenstein, komtur of Osterode, in August 1381. VLE and Wigand name no informant, so the name is one of several versions (`books/sources.qmd`). Not to be confused with Kuno von Lichtenstein, the Grand Commander killed at Grunwald.
- **[Saga invention]:** Nothing beyond the warning; the saga keeps the historical informant and does not turn him into a character of the Book VI cast.

## Pronunciation

**LEE-ben-shtine** · IPA /ˈliːbn̩ʃtaɪn/ · English sound-alike "LEE-ben-shtine". German; the Lithuanian text writes Kuno fon Liebensteinas (KOO-no fon LEE-ben-shtine-ahs). Not in the pronunciation lexicon; derived from its conventions for German names (compare Rotenstein).

## Appearances

- **Book I:** ch. 1.
- **Book VI:** the afterword (`istorine_pastaba.qmd`).

Continuity: earlier drafts and some canon documents name Günther von Hohenstein (the real Osterode komtur, d. 1380) as the informant; the fact-check pass replaced him with Liebenstein in Book I ch. 1.
